record.paper_title: Several Open Problems on Banach Spaces (Castro Urdiales 2014)
record.original_question: Is every Schauder basis of ell_1 randomly unconditionally divergent? A basis is randomly unconditionally divergent when there is a constant K such that each vector norm is bounded by K times the average, over independent signs, of the norm of the corresponding signed partial sums in the basis expansion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a Schauder basis of the Banach space $\ell_1$, so that every $x\in \ell_1$ has a unique expansion $x = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n(x)\, e_n$ converging in norm. The basis $(e_n)$ is called randomly unconditionally divergent (RUD) if there exists a constant $K>0$ such that, for every $x\in \ell_1$,
$$\|x\| \;\le\; K \cdot \mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon}\Big\| \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n\, a_n(x)\, e_n \Big\|,$$
where $(\varepsilon_n)$ is a sequence of independent $\pm 1$-valued Rademacher random variables and $\mathbb{E}_\varepsilon$ denotes expectation with respect to the Haar (uniform) measure on $\{-1,+1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (equivalently, the supremum over finite partial sums is finite and controlled by $K$ times the average above).

Determine whether every Schauder basis of $\ell_1$ is randomly unconditionally divergent in this sense.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct search did not locate a published resolution of this specific question about whether every Schauder basis of $\ell_1$ is RUD. The general theory of RUC/RUD bases is developed in works by Garling, Wojtaszczyk and others, but no source verifying a positive or negative answer for $\ell_1$ was found, so the status is unknown.

status_evidence.title: Bases of random unconditional convergence in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses RUC and RUD bases and their duality.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework of RUC/RUD bases but does not settle the $\ell_1$ question.
